thread:
sam: heads up — since the 03:00 deploy i've seen intermittent DNS timeouts from model-worker pods. ~1.5% of generation calls fail with SERVFAIL and we get backpressure in the batcher.
anya: seeing the same in us-west-gpu pool. coreDNS latency spikes at p95 (~120ms) and node-local-dns evictions are through the roof. CPU on the node-local-daemon is 80%+ during the surge.
mike: any correlation with the GPU job burst? we had a large training -> serve wave at 03:02 (thousands of concurrent sidecars). node-local cache qps jumped to ~22k/s.
sam: yes, started exactly at the bulk rollout window. stacktrace shows retries then downstream timeouts -> job failures.
infra-bot: [alert] service=model-worker rate=error 1.3% SERVFAIL window=5m region=us-west-2 dashboard=https://grafana.internal/r/abc123
anya: i pulled a quick tcpdump from one affected node — seeing lots of DNS responses with TC set and a bunch of truncated UDP responses. suspecting packet fragmentation or MTU mismatch. snippet: ```15:34:22.123456 IP 10.0.1.12.42345 > 10.0.2.20.53: 12345+ A? weights.internal.example.com. (120) 15:34:22.123459 IP 10.0.2.20.53 > 10.0.1.12.42345: 12345 ServFail 0/0/0 (84)```
mike: we rolled newer hosts with MTU 9000 in a subset last week; older nodes are 1500. if path MTU isn't consistent, fragments could be dropped (esp. with RDMA overlay). can someone run `ip link show` on a few nodes?
liz: on a canary node (gpu-10): `ip link show eth0` -> mtu 1500. on the new nic hosts (gpu-38): `ip link show eth0` -> mtu 9000. also saw `ethtool -k eth0` shows GRO enabled on 9000-mtu nodes.
mike: aha — mixed-MTU across pods contacting the same node-local-dns leads to fragmentation when the DNS response is larger (EDNS0, DNSSEC, long TXT records). if fragments don't make it back we get truncated/servfail symptoms. RDMA overlay might be clamping or dropping fragments.
anya: we also saw node-local-dns eviction logs: `evicting entry due to pressure: total_entries=20000, max=20000`. config map for node-local-dns uses small cache size (default 10k) and aggressive ttl. pods are creating lots of unique lookups (per-request hostnames for weights versioning).
sam: mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily reduce EDNS max-udp-size to 1232 on CoreDNS to avoid fragmentation, 2) bump node-local-dns cache size and eviction threshold, 3) roll back MTU change for the new hosts or enforce 9000 across the pool, 4) increase TCP fallback retries.
oncall: +1 to EDNS adjustment as a quick mitigation. can we patch corefile and roll to canary?
liz: patched coreDNS corefile on staging with `max_udp_size 1232` and `proxy` -> observed truncation->TCP fallback rate drop from 4% to 0.6% in 10m window. pushed same to a small canary in us-west and errors dropped.
mike: longer-term: standardize MTU on NICs, add e2e test for mixed-MTU, and update RDMA overlay config to not drop fragments (or add iptables rules). also consider increasing node-local-dns cache and enabling response compression if possible.
anya: filed infra ticket: https://tickets.internal/INFRA-8425 with notes + logs + recommended rollouts.
sam: assigning follow-ups: @mike MTU rollout rollback plan, @liz node-local-dns config bump and canary, @anya validate RDMA frag metrics. we'll reconvene after 1h. :thumbsup:
